AI search optimization in 2026 has evolved from ranking individual pages to establishing verifiable **entity authority** and optimizing content for **automated synthesis** [1-3]. The landscape is defined by a "triple threat" approach integrating traditional SEO, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) [4].

### Google AI Overviews and AI Mode: Source Selection and Fan-Out
Google operates three distinct AI surfaces: **AI Overviews (AIO)**, **Gemini**, and **AI Mode** [5].
*   **Source Selection:** Google selects citations through a multi-stage filtering pipeline that narrows **200–500 candidate documents** down to **5–15 cited sources** [6]. While mid-2025 data showed a **92% correlation** between the organic top 10 and AIO citations, by early 2026, this overlap dropped to approximately **38%**, with some analyses placing it as low as **14-17%** for AI Mode [1, 7-10].
*   **Query Fan-Out:** This mechanism expands a single user prompt into **5 to 11 sub-queries** on average to capture different intents [11, 12]. For complex tasks, research shows Google can fire **hundreds of parallel searches** [13].
*   **Concrete Tactic:** Sites with **80%+ topical coverage** of their domain retain **85.4% of AI visibility** despite fan-out instability, making comprehensive topic clusters more effective than keyword-specific pages [14, 15].

### Platform Citation Differences: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude
Each platform follows distinct retrieval logic:
*   **ChatGPT:** Draws heavily from **Bing-indexed content** and **Wikipedia** (which accounts for **47.9% of referrals**) [16-18]. It tends to cite lower-ranking pages, with roughly **90% of citations** coming from pages ranked **21 or lower** in traditional Google results [16].
*   **Perplexity:** Favors **real-time web search** and community sources [16, 19]. **Reddit** accounts for nearly half of its top citations, compared to under 10% for ChatGPT [16]. It has the strongest **recency bias**; content older than **90 days** loses priority for fast-moving queries [20, 21].
*   **Gemini:** Pulls roughly **43% of citations** from Google.com properties and **21% from Reddit** [19, 22]. It integrates deeply with **Google Workspace** (Gmail, Docs, Drive) to influence procurement decisions [7, 23].
*   **Claude:** Functions as a **reasoning engine** with a context window of up to **200,000+ tokens**, favoring long-form, comprehensive "Definitive Guides" and academic-style signals [24-26].

### llms.txt and Machine-Readable Files
*   **The Reality:** `llms.txt` is a **proposed Markdown map** for AI agents, not a standard or an access control [27-29]. **Google explicitly ignores it**, stating it provides "no measured reason" for citation gains [30-32].
*   **Utility:** Adoption sits around **10% of domains** [33, 34]. Its real value is limited to **developer documentation** and sites serving AI coding assistants like **Cursor** or **Claude Code**, where it reduces context window noise [35-37].
*   **Vendor Disagreement:** While SEO vendors like **AuditZap** and **CapstonAI** offer `llms.txt` generators/checkers, **Google** has compared the file to the long-discredited keywords meta tag [30, 38-40].

### AI Crawler Access and Control
The major shift in 2026 is the split between **training** and **search** crawlers [41, 42].
*   **The Split:** OpenAI uses **GPTBot** for training and **OAI-SearchBot** for search [43, 44]. Anthropic uses **ClaudeBot** (training) and **Claude-SearchBot** (search) [43, 45].
*   **Thresholds:** Anthropic’s crawl-to-referral ratio peaked at **70,900:1** in mid-2025, compared to traditional **Googlebot’s 5:1** [46-48].
*   **Enforcement:** **Robots.txt is voluntary** and not a technical lock [49, 50]. Hard enforcement requires **WAF/firewall rules** or **Server-level IP blocks**, as a WAF rule is enforced *before* robots.txt is read [51-53].
*   **Tool Names:** **Cloudflare AI Crawl Control** and **Kinsta Bot Protection** provide one-click toggles to block training bots while keeping search bots open [52, 54, 55].

### Entity SEO and Knowledge Graphs
Entity SEO established itself as a "durability requirement" following **June 2025**, when Google removed over **3 billion entities** (6.26% of the Knowledge Graph) to prioritize a leaner, higher-quality dataset [56-58].
*   **Knowledge Graph Stats:** The graph now contains over **1.6 trillion facts** about **54 billion entities** [59, 60].
*   **Concrete Tactic:** Use the **`sameAs`** property in `Organization` schema to link to **Wikidata Q-numbers**, **Crunchbase**, and **LinkedIn** [61-63]. Wikidata is often the most direct path to a Knowledge Panel for brands without a Wikipedia page [64, 65].
*   **Entity Recognition Lag:** Wikidata recognition is **fastest**; schema disambiguation is **fast**; Knowledge Panel triggering is **slower**; and Wikipedia inclusion is **slowest** [66, 67].

### Brand Mentions as a Visibility Lever
Branded web mentions have become a primary visibility signal, rivaling or exceeding backlinks for AI search [68, 69].
*   **Evidence:** A 2025 analysis found branded mentions correlate at **r = 0.664** with AIO citations, compared to **r = 0.218** for traditional backlinks [3, 70].
*   **Strategy:** Brands appearing on **four or more third-party platforms** are **2.8x more likely** to be cited in ChatGPT [71].
*   **Speculation vs. Evidence:** The **Princeton GEO Study** provided real evidence for content modifiers: adding **expert quotes** (+41%), **statistics** (+30%), and **inline citations** (+30%) measurably boosts citation probability [72-74]. Claims that branded mentions replace links are supported by independent studies (Semrush), but link-building remains the foundation for **getting into the candidate pool** that the AI eventually synthesizes [3, 75].

### Summary of Evidence vs. Speculation (2026)
| Feature | Evidence Level | Specific 2026 Data / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mention Correlation** | **High** | 0.664 correlation vs 0.218 for links (Semrush) [3, 70]. |
| **Princeton GEO Tactics** | **High** | +41% lift from expert quotes/citations [72, 76]. |
| **llms.txt Utility** | **Low/Speculative** | ~10% adoption; Google calls it "unnecessary" [32, 34, 77]. |
| **Query Fan-Out Scale** | **Medium** | 5-11 sub-queries average; hundreds for Deep Search [11, 12]. |
| **AIO Click Impact** | **High** | 58-61% drop in top-ranking page CTR [74, 78]. |
| **Entity Pruning** | **Medium (Vendor Study)** | 3 billion entities removed in one week (Ahrefs/Outpace) [56, 57]. |
